Banner

One message about the state of the whole app, across the full width under the app header.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For a condition that affects every screen and is still true, such as a lost connection, a paused agent host or a session about to end.
  • Directly under the app header, across the full width, for as long as the condition lasts.
  • With one action when there is one thing the reader can do about it, such as Retry.

When not to use it

  • For the result of something the reader just did, such as Task saved. Confirm it where it happened, or use a toast.
  • For a problem with one field or one form. Use the field's error message.
  • For a problem with one item in a view, such as a failed run. Show it on that item.
  • For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.
  • For more than one message at a time. Show the most severe one.

Variants

info
The default, with no modifier class. Something the reader should know that needs no action, such as a planned restart or a restored connection. Set role="status".
warning ds-banner--warning
Something is degraded or about to go wrong and the app is still usable, such as Reconnecting. Set role="status".
danger ds-banner--danger
Something has failed and work is blocked until it is fixed. Set role="alert".

Sizes

default
At least 44px tall and as wide as its container. The text wraps, and on a narrow screen the action and the dismiss button move below it.

Accessibility

  • Set role="status" on an info or warning banner, so a screen reader announces it when the reader pauses. Set role="alert" on a danger banner, so it is announced at once.
  • Keep the banner element in the page and change its text, or add the banner with its text already in it. Either way the message is announced once.
  • Do not set aria-busy on the banner. A screen reader holds back the announcement of a busy region. While the action runs, set aria-busy="true" on the action button and change its label, such as Retrying.
  • The stylesheet draws the tone's icon, so the tone never depends on colour and needs no markup. The text carries the whole message.
  • The action and the dismiss button sit together in a ds-banner__actions element after the text. The action is one ds-button ds-button--small, with a label that says what it does. Do not make it primary.
  • The dismiss button is a button with aria-label="Dismiss", and its icon carries aria-hidden="true". Offer it only when the message is safe to lose. When it is pressed, move focus to the main content.
  • Tab reaches the action and then the dismiss button, in that order. Enter and Space press them.
  • The banner does not take focus when it appears, so it never interrupts typing.
